new_entities.name: Panax ginseng supplementation
new_entities.description: Supplementation with Panax ginseng root preparations, including standardized Korean red ginseng extracts.

new_entities.name: Subjective fatigue
new_entities.description: Patient-reported fatigue severity assessed with validated subjective fatigue scales.

edges.effect_quant: A 2016 meta-analysis found a modest pooled fatigue benefit from ginseng supplements overall (SMD 0.34, 95% CI 0.16 to 0.52), but later Panax ginseng trials in chronic fatigue and advanced cancer have produced null or equivocal results.
edges.population: adults with chronic fatigue, rheumatic disease, or cancer-related fatigue
edges.mechanism: Panax ginseng is thought to affect fatigue through adaptogenic, anti-inflammatory, and neuroendocrine pathways that might modestly improve energy perception or recovery from stress. In practice, subjective fatigue is highly placebo-sensitive, and the human trial record shows heterogeneity across disease context, dose, and formulation.
edges.summary: Panax ginseng for subjective fatigue is better described as mixed than clearly effective. Pooled evidence suggests a small average anti-fatigue signal, but several modern placebo-controlled trials have found little or no meaningful advantage over placebo in the populations that most want this benefit.
edges.caveats: This literature mixes different ginseng species, doses, extracts, and fatigue syndromes, which makes the headline claim easy to oversimplify. Where benefit exists, it appears modest and context-dependent rather than uniformly reliable.

evidence.citation: Bae SM et al 2016 J Korean Med Sci
evidence.notes: Efficacy of Ginseng Supplements on Fatigue and Physical Performance: a Meta-analysis.
